subject: HorizonPay post-demo: model risk checklist & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Laura Jensen <laura@horizonpay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-15T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: HorizonPay post-demo: model fit & follow-ups

Hi Laura —

Thanks again for taking the demo. Quick recap and the two obvious follow-ups we promised: a short recommended-model plan for your use case (invoices + dispute triage), and a short note on how we protect you from surprise quality regressions when models update.

What we saw in the call: HorizonPay needs sub-400ms median LLM latency for single-turn vendor classification, deterministic entity extraction for refund reasons, and a high recall on dispute-related prompts. You also called out an internal requirement to pin inference behavior during pilot windows and to be able to revert quickly if you observe regressions.

Recommended short-list (based on the small benchmark we ran during the call):
- redwood-gpt-7b-q4a (low-cost, high throughput) — good for high-volume classification and structured extraction.
- redwood-cli-13b-fp16 (higher fidelity) — better at edge-case language in merchant disputes.
- open-xl-8b-quant (experimental) — higher precision on niche legal language but will need prompt conditioning.

I attached the prompt-set (horizon-demo-prompt-set_v1.csv) we used and the quick benchmark summary (hp-benchmark-summary-20270415.pdf). The Drive link in Related Links has the full perf traces and token-level cost simulation.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Can you confirm pilot target volumes (qps / peak per minute) and the compliance scope (PCI-scope only vs. broader PII)? That will determine whether we recommend dedicated capacity for the pilot.
2) How comfortable is Horizon with a pinned model during pilot weeks vs. automatic minor-variant updates?
3) If you want, Ben can run a 24-hour synthetic regression run against your top 5 prompt variants and surface delta reports.

I'll leave Ben and Rishi on the thread for the technical pin/rollback details. If you'd like a succinct mutual action plan doc, I can draft one by Friday.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: horizon-demo-prompt-set_v1.csv (CSV), hp-benchmark-summary-20270415.pdf (PDF)

Marissa —

Really helpful, thanks. A couple quick answers and one urgent question from procurement:
- Pilot target: 50 qps sustained, spikes to 300 qps for heavy batch windows (end-of-day reconciliation).
- Compliance: PCI-scope for the pilot, broader PII controls required for production.

Procurement asks: if we pin a model during the pilot, what is the rollback SLA and what visibility do we get into model-version diffs if we detect a regression? We need ability to revert within a 2 hour window and an audit trail for any version change.

Also, can you confirm whether pinning incurs a pricing premium vs. standard hosted usage? If so, what’s the delta?

Looping in our contracts team (contracts@horizonpay.com) for timeline.

Thanks,
Laura
Director, Integrations
Horizon Payments

On Thu, Apr 16, 2027 at 9:02 AM Laura Jensen <laura@horizonpay.com> wrote:
> Marissa —
> 
> Really helpful, thanks. A couple quick answers and one urgent question from procurement:
> - Pilot target: 50 qps sustained, spikes to 300 qps for heavy batch windows (end-of-day reconciliation).
> - Compliance: PCI-scope for the pilot, broader PII controls required for production.

Thanks — notes below and a technical plan for the pin/rollback path.

Quick technical notes:
- For 50 qps sustained and 300 spikes we recommend dedicated pools during pilot unless Horizon is comfortable with burst rules on hosted capacity. Dedicated will give the predictable latency you asked for and clean tenancy for PCI.
- Pinning options: we support two styles — (A) "soft pin" (lock major version, allow minor patching that is backward compatible) and (B) "hard pin" (freeze exact model artifact by build hash). For pilot I recommend hard pin for the first 2 weeks.
- Rollback SLA: we can revert a hard pin to the previous artifact within 30 minutes if we have the revert approval from Horizon. We keep immutable artifacts and commit hashes in our registry for audit. Example artifact ids: redwood-gpt-7b-q4a@sha256:3f9a8c4 and redwood-cli-13b-fp16@sha256:ad4e7b1.
- Diff reporting: we provide a delta report (token-level output differences + prompt-set fail-rate) produced by our regression harness. We'll include the report link and an S3 snapshot for your audit trail.

Cost note on pinning: hard-pinning to a dedicated pool carries an allocation premium (we charge for reserved capacity + a small stability add-on). For a 2-week hard pin on a pool sized for 50 qps, rough estimate: $9k-$11k/week depending on region and GPU mix. I will formalize this with an ABAC cost sheet and put it into the deal record.

Proposed immediate actions (technical):
1) Run a 24-hour synthetic regression run against horizon-demo-prompt-set_v1.csv. I can have results in ~48 hours.
2) Prepare a pinning-options-matrix.xlsx (attached) with the fail-open/fail-closed behaviors we discussed.
3) If Horizon approves, we create a dedicated pool and hard-pin the artifact redwood-gpt-7b-q4a@sha256:3f9a8c4 for the initial pilot window.

Ben Carter
Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: pinning-options-matrix.xlsx
